Committing to this repo requires conforming messages and structure-clean code: type(scope): subject ≤72 chars; fix commits need Regression/Class/Sweep trailers (class from .mivia/quality/defect-taxonomy.md, e.g. DC-13); pre-commit runs check_go_structure.py --strict --staged where soft limits (500 file/80 func/800 test-file) become hard — no --no-verify, no baseline raises.

The workspace enforces these gates via scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit and pre-push; knowing them upfront avoids failed-commit round trips and accidental capture of a peer agent's work. scope: project

tags: workflows, delivery, allow-publish, session-engine, restart
created: 2026-08-12

## Summary
Delivery authorization for harness auto-delivery comes from the workflow's [delivery] policy, never from caller-side allow_publish (which is not persisted). A session-start sweep (workflowToolServiceWithBus, provider != nil) publishes delivery_pending runs left over from a restart/crash; the settlement repair loop ignores allow_publish.

## What worked
- Reused the claim/flock machinery: reconcile serializes per-run via beginWorkflowExecution, so it never races a live deliverer
- provider != nil (event bus) cleanly discriminates production wiring from tests
- deliverRunWithStore already refuses runs without an active delivery policy, so the sweep cannot over-publish

## What did not work
- Caller-side allow_publish was never persisted anywhere, so no post-restart sweep could be authorized before this change

## Why
Runs park at delivery_pending only when their workflow declares a delivery policy, so that policy is the only durable grant. The old design required allow_publish=true at admission (caller-side, unpersisted); after a restart no post-restart path had authorization, stranding 5 runs (wfr-5RUOSMJHUWHJXSNH, wfr-BBFPZLL7PUTX6WXX, ...) until manual `workflow deliver --allow-publish`. Fixed in e4287c13: sessionAutoDeliveryRepairLoop drops the flag gate, and a one-shot reconcile publishes parked runs at session wiring.

# Orchestration guardrails: sub-agents stall without committing

scope: project
verdict: mixed
tags: orchestration, spawn_agent, guardrails, commit-discipline, concurrent-writer
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Spawned go-engineer agents stalled twice on multi-feature tasks: s3 looped 30+ min on test fixes without committing; s5 ended its run having staged (git add) but never committed. Both required root takeover to finalize. Hard guardrails fixed it: commit-first-green, hard time-boxes (20-25 min), max 2 fix attempts then stop-and-report.

## What worked
- Commit-first-green guardrail produced fast, clean commits (s6b done in 2 min)
- Steer with interrupt=true successfully broke s3 out of its loop
- Checking git status + staged diff at run end recovered s5's staged work
- Full-tree fresh verification (go test -count=1 ./...) caught everything before reporting done

## What did not work
- s3 ran 30+ min with no commit, no parks, no retries — silent spin
- s5 staged its commit but the task completed without finalizing it
- Docs agent never committed its deliverables (had to be committed by root)
- Event ledger records only start events; completion is invisible there — git log is ground truth

## Why
Large spawned tasks (controller admission, driver CLI) loop silently on failing tests — no parks/retries/blocked events appear, so the event ledger gives no signal. Work is at risk from a concurrent writer that restores older file snapshots; uncommitted files can vanish. Root must verify git status + index state at run end, not just task statuses: staged-but-uncommitted work is common (s5 staged 1356 lines then ended). Always include explicit commit instructions in every task prompt (docs agents won't commit otherwise) and re-verify the final tree yourself.

## References
- none

# Panel review context: recency ordering + cap tightening (research-backed)

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: panel, context, review, lost-in-the-middle, workflows
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Context management for panel reviews: reordered the 6 panel member templates so instructions lead and the review target (findings + implementation) sits at the end (recency beats lost-in-the-middle), and tightened bug-fix.toml binding caps (scope 4K, findings 16K). Members already use the industry-standard patterns (structured outputs, parallel specialization, selective fetch).

## What worked
- Template text controls binding render order (template.Render expands {{ }} in file order): "lost in the middle" (arXiv 2307.03172) is fixable by reordering sections — instructions first, review target (findings/implementation) last, plan in the middle
- Envelope-only bindings (prior_findings 4096B) are the established sharing mechanism; step-level bindings feed ALL panel members + the post-panel review step (do not remove them as "dead" — synthesis just doesn't render them)
- Members already follow the industry pattern: structured JSON output schemas, parallel domain specialization, selective file fetch via read tools (diff-only + fetch)
- Tightened bug-fix.toml caps: scope 16000→4096, findings 32768→16384 (worst-case reduction; typical content unaffected)
- Contract tests assert member config paths only, not template content — template reordering is test-safe

## What did not work
- Compaction/summarization is lossy and compounds (Claude Code ~20K token summary reservation; Codex compaction fragile) — use as last resort, not primary strategy
- Per-member binding scoping (security gets no plan) is an engine change (step-level bindings are shared) — deferred
- "Avrix" is NOT a code review product; only an AI-infrastructure firm (avrix.com) — user likely meant Aider/CodeRabbit-class tools

## Why
Industry research (Claude Code/Aider/Cline/Codex/Cursor + G-Research, arXiv 2307.03172) shows focused prompts beat long ones and the most important content must be at the start/end. Our pipeline already had structured context, envelopes, and per-member specialization; the two real wins were ordering and worst-case caps. Compaction was rejected as lossy; per-member binding scoping deferred (engine change).

scope: project

tags: workflows, stacking, delivery, diff-size, correction
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
CORRECTION: on_diff_size_failure is a [delivery] repair-STEP name, never a dead-fail enum. An over-limit diff is a repairable DiffSizeError routed to the repair step (fallback on_failure): the agent shrinks/splits the chunk, delivery retries, bounded by max_repairs. The run is never failed for size alone.

## What worked
- Verified ground truth in code before answering: types.go Delivery.OnDiffSizeFailure (step name), delivery/repair.go RepairTarget (DiffSizeError -> OnDiffSizeFailure -> OnFailure), delivery/stacking.go checkChunkDiffSize (repairable DiffSizeError), controller linear_diff_gate.go (post-implement reroute to the repair step).
- Corrected docs/architecture/workflows.md + docs/product/workflows-guide.md (removed the bogus [stacking] key; added the [delivery] table row).
- Strengthened repair.md + bugfix-repair.md: a DIFF-SIZE rejection is a SPLIT request - shrink the delivered diff, record deferred scope in summary for a follow-up chunk, never silently drop scope.

## What did not work
- My earlier summary/memory claimed an enum on_diff_size_failure = shrink_retry|reroute_fail_fast with a dead-fail mode. That enum DOES NOT EXIST in the code: on_diff_size_failure is a [delivery] knob naming a repair STEP (same pattern as on_failure/on_pr_metadata_failure). The docs I wrote for it were wrong and have been corrected.
- A single inline run can only SHRINK its own delivered diff; turning deferred scope into additional PRs is the stacking driver's (mivia stack plan/drive) job - be explicit about that boundary rather than implying a single run re-chunks.

## Why
The user caught a real misinformation bug: my docs/summary claimed the system can dead-fail a run for an oversized PR, which is the opposite of what the code does and of what they asked for. Recording the verified semantics prevents repeating the error and documents the honest boundary (single-run shrink vs driver-driven multi-PR breakdown).

- Verified executable checks: YAML parse OK, bash -n OK, py_compile OK, make release-test PASS, go run ./cmd/mivia version --json returns {"binary":"mivia","version":"0.0.0-dev"} matching the workflow assertions

Records the verified state of the release pipeline so future release work starts from facts: tag-driven flow, review verdict, advisory status of pins (correcting the non-existent CVE-2025-26367/30226 premises). Hostile audit loop ran 7 rounds; zero confirmed bugs at the end.

- Resolve-once + pin-every-dial (newLoopbackDialContext) defeats DNS rebinding; redirects and HTTPS go through the same pinned dial (DialTLSContext stays nil)
- Non-vacuous test discipline: F1-F10 coverage tests verified by branch-removal reasoning; vacuous tests caught and fixed (error-text discriminators)

The security-critical design: mode inference from base_url must be literal-only (no DNS in the predicate), keyless construction must resolve every localhost address to loopback at construction and pin all dials (redirects, HTTPS, retries) to those IPs, and every relaxed gate must be conjunctive (provider name AND loopback) so non-ollama providers never lose their key/HTTPS requirements. summary: On Windows, cmd/go locates its build cache via GOCACHE or %LocalAppData%\go-build. A filtered env for go subprocesses that drops LOCALAPPDATA (and lacks GOCACHE, which go test never exports) makes every `go list`/packages.Load die with "build cache is required, but could not be located", yielding zero packages — misreported as "symbol not found". # Windows go subprocess needs LOCALAPPDATA passthrough in filtered env

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: windows, packages.Load, GOCACHE, environment-filtering, codeintel, wine
created: 2026-08-10

## Summary
On Windows, cmd/go locates its build cache via GOCACHE or %LocalAppData%\go-build. A filtered env for go subprocesses that drops LOCALAPPDATA (and lacks GOCACHE, which go test never exports) makes every `go list`/packages.Load die with "build cache is required, but could not be located", yielding zero packages — misreported as "symbol not found". Unix masks it via $HOME/.cache/go-build.

## What worked
- Reproduced the CI failure under wine with a real GOOS=windows test binary; the Linux ELF "probe" binary had silently run natively, not under wine (checked with `file`).\n- Driver-level probe (exec go list with the filtered env) surfaced the exact error text instead of guessing.\n- EqualFold matching for Windows env keys avoids the case trap (LOCALAPPDATA vs LocalAppData).

## What did not work
- First attempt added "LocalAppData" (title case) to the allowlist — did nothing because the real var is LOCALAPPDATA.\n- Debugging through the analyzer's "symbol not found" error wasted time; the load errors are swallowed by design.

## Why
internal/codeintel/analyzerEnv() filtered os.Environ() to a small allowlist to block network access. The allowlist had "LocalAppData" (title case) while Windows sets LOCALAPPDATA, so the variable was dropped; all codeintel symbol queries then failed on Windows CI while passing on Linux/macOS. Fix: pass LOCALAPPDATA through with case-insensitive (EqualFold) matching. Also: `go test` does NOT export GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE/GOROOT to test binaries (verified empirically), and `go test -c` without GOOS=windows builds a HOST (Linux) binary even with a .exe name — verify with `file` before running under wine.

## What worked
- Live smoke caught the bug unit tests missed: reviewer output describing a TEST FIXTURE (temp dir containing .mivia/workflows) tripped the demand-verb heuristic.

- Line-wide "path token + demand verb on same line" over-matches prose that quotes paths descriptively.

scope: project

## Summary
Fixed the delivery-repair death loop: the stacking auto-split and the repair agent's deferred_files can no longer defer a file's tests while shipping its code (or vice versa) - both are refused with a repairable DiffSizeError, and a pre-push rejection is led by a delivered-commit inventory hint so the repair agent can tell stale-tree rejection from real code rejection.

## What worked
- Guarded both split paths with the same companion rule: checkChunkDiffSize (auto split, stacking.go) and guardDeferredSplitConsistency (repair agent's deferred_files, deliver_split_guard.go) - helpers deferredSplitSeparatesCompanion/testCompanions/subtractPaths are language-agnostic (*_test, *.test, *_spec, *.spec, test_*, Test* same-directory).
- deliveryInventoryHint (deliver_hint.go) is prepended to the recorded push-failure text BEFORE the hook rejection (markFailed truncates from the end, so it must lead) and lists delivered-commit files, deferred files, and worktree-only changes; the deferred section is git-independent (reads req.Inputs then the existing record).
- Resume refusal now names BOTH the recorded deferred files and the currently staged files (deliver_split_resume.go).
- Structure gate: extracted the guard helpers and the deferred follow-up commit (commitDeferredFollowUp) so stacking.go and freshDeliveryCommitSplit stay under the 500/80 LOC soft limits.

## What did not work
- search_replace refused to delete the trailing helper block because its idempotency heuristic saw the new_string ("return files, total, nil }\n") already present as a substring of the still-present block; worked around by replacing with a pointer comment, then the same old_string match succeeded (the first attempt at the identical edit had silently no-op'd in multi_edit).
- The auto-split is greedy largest-first; a rare case can refuse a split even when a non-separating split exists (repair round trip then shrinks it) - safe but not optimal; documented trade-off.

## Why
The observed death loop: the auto split deferred a file's tests to the follow-up PR while the code stayed in the delivered commit; the pre-push hook then tested a stale/partial tree and rejected, and the repair agent kept reverting production code to satisfy the delivered commit's stale test expectations. The guard makes a delivered commit internally consistent by construction, and the inventory hint tells the agent which tree the hook verified.

feature-delivery runs settle at delivery_pending and only publish when the host calls workflow_deliver(allow_publish=true) — publication is never implicit. # Stacking workflows: synthesize run graph BEFORE the runtime build (empty routing digest bug)

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: workflows, stacking, routing-digest, admission, bugfix
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Stacking runs failed at their first synthesized step with "agent task routing snapshot mismatch": the controller synthesized the graph AFTER the runtime build and, lacking a registry, injected runtimes with an EMPTY digest. Fix: synthesize before building step runtimes wherever the registry exists (cli, localengine); controller now refuses admission for missing/digest-less synthesized steps.

## What worked
- Made compiler.SynthesizeStacking idempotent (both synthesized steps + repair loop present => already synthesized).
- Synthesized in cli buildWorkflowController and localengine (fresh + resume) before the runtime build, so decompose/chunk_plan_validate get full registry-resolved runtimes (digest, template, schema) and are pinned into the run snapshot for resume.
- Replaced controller-side runtime fabrication with requireSynthesizedStepRuntimes: admission refuses a synthesized step with a missing or digest-less runtime.
- Regression tests: controller admission guard, CLI runtime pinning, resume round-trip, e2e buildWorkflowController.

## What did not work
- Old design injected synthesized runtimes into the controller without a digest; the agent-handler guard caught it at execution ("routing snapshot mismatch") but the run was already admitted and died mid-flight.
- Controller tests with scripted runners that never validate digests could not see the bug; only a path through the real registry-resolving build would have caught it.
- Edge case: a workflow declaring ALL THREE engine-reserved identifiers (decompose + chunk_plan_validate + decompose_repair) is treated as already-synthesized (documented).

## Why
The controller has no agent registry, so it can never resolve a routing digest — synthesizing there is architecturally impossible to do correctly. Any future entry point that builds StepRuntime maps must synthesize the stacking graph first (compiler.SynthesizeStacking is idempotent via the triple reserved-id check). Test coverage must include a path where registry-resolved digests reach a digest-validating handler; scripted runners that never validate digests cannot see this bug class.

title: Pin defensive Go error branches: closed DB, connector wrapper, ENAMETOOLONG, chmod
summary: Proven patterns for covering otherwise-unreachable error/edge branches in Go tests: closed *sql.DB for generic statement errors, custom driver.Connector wrapping modernc sqlite to fail one statement, directory-in-place-of-file for read errors, >255-char path component for non-IsNotExist stat errors, chmod 0555 for RemoveAll failure.
content:
# Pin defensive Go error branches: closed DB, connector wrapper, ENAMETOOLONG, chmod

scope: project
verdict: neutral
tags: go, testing, coverage, sqlite, modernc, error branches
created: 2026-08-16

## Summary
Proven patterns for covering otherwise-unreachable error/edge branches in Go tests: closed *sql.DB for generic statement errors, custom driver.Connector wrapping modernc sqlite to fail one statement, directory-in-place-of-file for read errors, >255-char path component for non-IsNotExist stat errors, chmod 0555 for RemoveAll failure.

## What worked
- Closed pool: `sql.Open(...)`, `db.Close()`, then `&SQLite{db: db}` - every statement errors with "sql: database is closed", covering generic error returns (pattern already used in plan57_diff_coverage_test.go).
- Custom connector: implement driver.Connector wrapping `(&sqlite3.Driver{}).Open(dsn)`; override QueryContext/ExecContext to fail when query contains a substring, and Close to return an injected error - hits branches a live DB can never reach (e.g. UPDATE succeeds with 0 rows, then the follow-up SELECT fails).
- Non-IsNotExist stat error: write a gitdir pointer whose path component is 300 chars -> os.Stat returns ENAMETOOLONG; root-proof.
- RemoveAll failure: chmod 0555 the dir (skip as root); register a cleanup chmod 0755 so t.TempDir cleanup works.
- Read error after successful open: replace a file with a directory -> io.ReadAll returns EISDIR.
- Resolve via `git worktree list` skips registrations with unparseable pointers - assert the admin registration directory still exists instead.

## What did not work
- Trying to force the follow-up SELECT failure via real SQLite states (dropped tables, views, triggers) never works because the preceding UPDATE fails first - only a statement-targeted connector wrapper reaches it.
- sql.DB.Close() effectively never returns non-nil with modernc; you must inject the driver-level Close error via the connector wrapper.

## Why
The diff-coverage gate demands a zero-hit count on every changed statement line, including defensive branches no live database or filesystem state can reach. These patterns are the repo's established way to pin them (schemaErrorDriver, plan57 tests).

## References
- none

# Stacking plan-run publication is opt-in via delivery.deliver_plan_run (default false)

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: workflows, stacking, delivery, plan-run, config
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
A stacking plan run is the stack root, not a deliverable: after its chunk stack drives, the plan run settles succeeded and is NOT published unless the workflow sets delivery.deliver_plan_run=true. Plan and artifacts stay in the ledger either way.

## What worked
- Default-false bool keeps existing stacking workflows' behavior unchanged\n- CLI and session surfaces both route through one compiledDeliverPlanRun check\n- Tests: workflow_stack_drive_order_test.go covers CLI + session + drive contract for both settings

## What did not work
- parseRunLine had to change from first-match to last-match; any code assuming the first run_id line is the final state would misread the skip path

## Why
Drive-before-delivery ordering is load-bearing: a multi-chunk plan run settles at delivery_pending (delivery-policy active success terminal), so the chunk stack must drive BEFORE the delivery branch or the plan PR publishes and the stack never drives. The deliver_plan_run option (types.go Delivery struct, toml key) resolves via compiledDeliverPlanRun for the CLI path and is passed into sessionAutoDeliveryRepairLoop for the session path. The skip path CASes the run to succeeded via settlePlanRunSkippedDelivery and prints a second run_id/status line - parseRunLine now takes the LAST such line. Session UI gets run_finished via publishSkippedPlanRunFinished keyed on the seeded stack task ledger (ReadBackPlan), since no delivery record exists.

- Verified the design in internal/cli/session_delivery_repair.go.

## What did not work
- workflow_deliver against the held flock returns 'lock is busy' - expected, no value.

## Why
Prevents misreading a parked delivery_pending run as stuck and forcing delivery (bypasses deliver-before-drive ordering). Observed: plan run wfr-inv-20dbb0f9 parked while the chunk stack ran and failed.
